analysis: Rigidity test - the 3 shortest laws of every infinite non-trivial affine class (147 laws from the 56 classes, selected by the Q-gcd of the affine system), all affine tables blocked, N = 2..8. 146 laws have non-affine anchored models, all at every N = 6, 7, 8; only x((yz)z) = z((yx)x) (affine system 2a^2 - 1) is rigid on the tested range; 0 UNKNOWN instances. H-C13-2 refuted. (Corrected after the Skeptic's review - the first run selected classes by a spectrum heuristic that also let in 52 laws from 23 finite classes Div(L), L >= 61, and reported 198 of 199 non-rigid with 12 UNKNOWN instances, all of them in finite-class laws.) The short laws of each class are weak (e.g. x = x(x(xx)) constrains only diagonals). A first run with 4 laws per class, N <= 9 and budget 2,000,000 was stopped after 17 CPU-minutes.

hypothesis: H-C13-2 (bold): for every law with at most 4 leaves per side (3 variables) or 5 leaves per side (2 variables) whose affine spectrum is infinite and not all N, every anchored model is affine.
methodology: For each selected law and N, add one blocking clause per affine table x + a*y + 1 to the anchored SAT encoding; SAT means a non-affine model exists (the table is recorded for N <= 5), UNSAT means every model is affine.
question: For laws whose affine spectrum is infinite but not all N (golden, x^2+x+1, -1 square, 2 square, odd, plastic, tribonacci, ...), does every anchored model of size N <= 8 come from an affine table x*y = x + a*y + 1? If so, the true spectrum agrees with the arithmetic set for N <= 8.
